Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

Coffee Shop & Cocktail Bar at Quarry Trails Metro Park, Columbus

Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails is the only café-bar in Columbus sitting inside a Metro Park — serving bold espresso, craft cocktails, and fresh food with an unobstructed view of Quarry Trails Lake. Whether you’re coming off the trails, heading out for an evening, or just want somewhere genuinely different to spend a few hours in West Columbus, this is the spot. Located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, we’re open seven days a week from morning coffee to last call.


Hours

Bold Coffee. Craft Cocktails. Metro Park Views.

The Quarry Trails location runs the full Bada Bean menu — locally roasted espresso, signature lattes, cold brew, and seasonal café drinks from open until 4 PM. When the bar takes over in the afternoon, the cocktail program steps up: craft originals, classic builds, and a rotating seasonal menu developed with local spirits and fresh ingredients.

We serve breakfast and lunch daily, with food from local purveyors and bar snacks as the evening kicks in. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 4–6 PM, with an extended hour from 6–7 PM for Thrive Card members. It’s one of the most distinctive happy hour settings in Columbus — lake on one side, cocktail in hand.

Dogs are welcome on the patio. If you’re hiking Quarry Trails Metro Park, we’re the obvious stop before or after.

Bada gift cards are now available.

Send instantly. Redeem easily. Perfect for anyone who loves coffee, cocktails, or both.

Buy Now

    • VIPS ONLY

    Bada at Quarry Trails is officially open—and the best is yet to come. Join our insider list for access to exclusive events, new menu drops, and VIP perks you won’t want to miss.

    Sign Up

    Parking

    Parking is available on the street and in the lot behind the Tillmore apartments. To unlock two free hours, fire up the ParkMobile app, enter the lot code, add your license plate, and confirm. Skipping this step might earn you a parking ticket, and nobody wants that.

    Open Map

    Weekly Events at Quarry Trails

    Quarry Trails hosts some of Bada Bean’s most popular recurring programming — and it’s a different lineup than you’ll find at our other Columbus locations:

    • Cosmos & Crafts — Every Wednesday, 4–10 PM. Bring your craft supplies, your creativity, and your appetite for a good Cosmo.
    • Off The Record: Jazz Night at the Quarry — Every Thursday, 7–9 PM. Live jazz, craft cocktails, and lake views. One of the best Thursday nights in Columbus.
    • Classic Movies & Cocktails — Every Friday, 4–10 PM. Classics on screen, great drinks in hand — the Quarry Trails signature Friday experience.
    • Trivia Night — Every Monday, 7–9 PM. Start your week with a little competition and happy hour pricing.

    Private events are available at Quarry Trails. The space is a standout venue for corporate gatherings, milestone celebrations, and private buyouts — with full café and bar service, Metro Park surroundings, and lake views that no ballroom in Columbus can match.

    Finding Bada Bean at Quarry Trails

    We’re located at 2157 Quarry Trails Drive, Suite A, Columbus, OH 43228, inside the Quarry Trails Metro Park community on Columbus’s west side. We’re easily accessible from Upper Arlington, Hilliard, and the broader West Columbus area.

    Parking: Free parking is available on the street and in the lot behind the Tillmore apartments. Use the ParkMobile app for two complimentary hours — enter the lot code, add your plate, and confirm before you walk in.

    FAQ

    Do you have free Wi-Fi?

    Yes, we offer complimentary Wi-Fi to all our guests. We kindly ask that you support our business by ordering food and beverages while enjoying this service.

    What food options are available at Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We offer a variety of food options, including pastries from Happy Little Treats and bar snacks in the evening. Our menu is carefully curated to complement our coffee and other beverages.

    What type of coffee does Bada Bean Bada Booze serve?

    We partner with local roasters to bring you the best flavors.

    Can I get espresso at any time of the day?

    To maintain a calming atmosphere in the evening, we stop serving espresso after 4 PM to avoid disrupting our workflow during busier bar hours.

    Does Bada Bean Bada Booze offer vegan or gluten-free options?

    Yes, we offer a selection of vegan and gluten-free items. Please ask our staff for specific options when you visit.

    Can I bring outside food into Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    Outside food is prohibited. If there’s an item you’d like to see on our menu, please fill out our digital comment card near the register to let us know!

    Do you offer the same products across all locations?

    Yes, we do. However, each location may have exclusive, secret menu beverages—get to know our team to discover these special items!

    What merchandise does Bada Bean Bada Booze sell?

    We offer a variety of merchandise, including branded apparel, mugs, and more. Check out our merch section in-store or online.

    Do I need to make a reservation?

    Reservations are not required, but they are recommended for larger groups or special events. You can make a reservation through our Private Events page.

    How can I partner with Bada Bean Bada Booze?

    We’re always open to partnerships! Please reach out to us via our contact form with your proposal or idea.

    Is Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails dog friendly?

    es — dogs are welcome on our patio at Quarry Trails. It’s one of the best dog-friendly café patios in Columbus, right alongside Quarry Trails Metro Park. Service animals only are permitted inside per health regulations.

    How can I stay updated on the latest news and promotions?

    Follow us on social media or sign up for our newsletter to stay in the loop about upcoming events, promotions, and new menu items.

    Do you sell Gift Cards

    Yes! Bada E-gift cards make a great gift. They are redeemable at any Bada location. Purchase yours here

    Is Bada Bean Bada Booze at Quarry Trails a good spot after hiking?

    It’s genuinely one of the best post-trail stops in Columbus. We’re located directly inside the Quarry Trails community, so you can go from the trails to an espresso or a cold cocktail with lake views in under five minutes. We serve food all day, so whether it’s a breakfast sandwich in the morning or bar snacks in the afternoon, we’ve got you covered.

event.title: Living History: The 1776 Gathering at Fort Pitt
event.categories_json: [{"name":"Featured","slug":"featured","term_group":0,"term_taxonomy_id":186,"taxonomy":"tribe_events_cat","description":"","parent":0,"count":225,"filter":"raw","term_order":"0","id":183,"urls":{"self":"https://www.heinzhistorycenter.org/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/categories/183","collection":"https://www.heinzhistorycenter.org/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/categories"}}]
event.description:
Discover the story of a pivotal 1776 conference that brought Continental Congress representatives and Native leaders together at Fort Pitt.

Join Fort Pitt Museum Living History Coordinator Lukas Smith and DJ Huff, a member of the Seneca Nation, as they commemorate the gathering with special living history presentations.

In October 1776, Jasper Yeates, a Pennsylvania lawyer appointed by the Continental Congress as a commissioner for Indian affairs, traveled to Fort Pitt to work alongside George Morgan, the Continental Congress’s Indian agent at Fort Pitt, and other commissioners. Together, they met with representatives of Native nations in the Ohio Country as American officials sought neutrality during the growing Revolutionary War.

Experience this moment in history with living history vignettes and musket and rifle demonstrations at 1, 2, and 3 p.m. on the Fort Pitt Museum lawn, weather permitting.

Admission

The living history vignettes and rifle demonstrations are free to attend. Regular admission applies to enter the museum and explore its exhibitions.

event.title: Walk in Penn’s Woods
event.description:
Explore Pennsylvania’s natural history on a guided woodland walk that connects the past to the present.

In partnership with the Pennsylvania Forestry Association, Penn State, the Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources, and other organizations across the commonwealth, Meadowcroft will host an immersive educational walk through its surrounding landscape.

Step into the footsteps of prehistoric hunter-gatherers and discover how early inhabitants relied on native plants and wildlife for food, tools, and survival. Along the way, learn how Pennsylvania’s forests have evolved over time and why they remain vital today.

Admission

Walk in Penn’s Woods is included with admission. Purchasing tickets in advance is encouraged, but tickets will also be sold at the admissions desk in the Barensfeld Center depending on availability.

event.categories_json: [{"name":"Featured","slug":"featured","term_group":0,"term_taxonomy_id":186,"taxonomy":"tribe_events_cat","description":"","parent":0,"count":225,"filter":"raw","term_order":"0","id":183,"urls":{"self":"https://www.heinzhistorycenter.org/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/categories/183","collection":"https://www.heinzhistorycenter.org/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/categories"}}]
event.description:
During this special panel discussion kicking off Italian Heritage Month, Anne Madarasz, director of the Franco Harris Sports Museum, and Melissa E. Marinaro, director of the Italian American Program, will join original members of Franco’s Italian Army and special guests to share stories and explore the group’s lasting cultural and social impact.

The program will not only remember and celebrate Franco’s Italian Army, but also reflect on issues related to ethnicity, identity, and the enduring legacy of the 1970s.

In 1972, Steelers rookie running back Franco Harris took the NFL by storm. A first-round draft pick, Harris finished the season with 1,055 rushing yards, a Pro Bowl nomination, and an NFL Rookie of the Year Award.

His breakout season inspired a new kind of Steelers fandom. That November, a group of fans traded black and gold for the green, white, and red Italian Tricolor and marched onto the scene as Franco’s Italian Army, just as the Steelers were battling for their first division championship in 1972.

Originally made up of second-generation Italian Americans from Pittsburgh’s East Liberty neighborhood, home to one of Pittsburgh’s historic Little Italies, the Army celebrated Franco’s heritage and reinforced their own ethnic pride and traditions in their Steelers fandom by including Italian food, wine, and gear in their game day traditions.

The Franco Harris Sports Museum’s annual Game Changers program explores the people, stories, and pivotal moments in Western Pennsylvania sports history that have transformed Pittsburgh and left a lasting impact beyond the playing field.

Admission

Tickets are $10 for non-members and $5 for History Center members.

event.description:
Join Fort Pitt Museum Living History Coordinator Lukas Smith for a look at the curious locals and travelers drawn to the site of the Battle of the Monongahela.

In July 1775, General Edward Braddock’s disastrous defeat on the banks of the Monongahela, present-day Braddock, Pa., marked a pivotal moment in Britain’s struggle with the French and their Native allies for control of the Forks of the Ohio.

But the battlefield’s story didn’t end with the fighting. For decades, the remains of Braddock’s soldiers lay improperly buried at the site, their bones attracting curious visitors and turning the battlefield into an early destination for “macabre tourism.”

Dig into the site’s grisly past during this spooky season edition of Speaker Saturday.

Admission

The program is included with regular admission and will take place in the Fort Pitt Auditorium on the museum’s first floor.

event.description:
In the 1970s,  Dr. Landers was part of the groundbreaking excavation team at Meadowcroft Rockshelter when archaeologists uncovered evidence of human habitation dating back nearly 19,000 years.

That discovery not only transformed history’s understanding of when people first arrived in North America; it marked the beginning of Dr. Lander’s remarkable 40-year career.

Join Dr. Landers in conversation with Dave Scofield, Director of Meadowcroft Rockshelter and Historic Village, as they discuss the discoveries that shaped her career and the people and places she encountered along the way.

Hear firsthand stories from her time at Meadowcroft and behind-the-scenes insights from a career spent uncovering the past.

Before the program, explore Planet Ice: Mysteries of the Ice Ages on the History Center’s first floor. The exhibit features authentic Paleoindian tools and artifacts from Meadowcroft, including an elk tooth and passenger pigeon bones recovered from the Rockshelter.

Admission

Admission is $10 for non-members and $5 for members. The program will take place in the museum’s fifth floor Mueller Center.

American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation will be available upon request. Please contact us at programs@heinzhistorycenter.org in advance to request accommodations.

About Dr. Landers

Dr. Diane Beynon Landers is a seasoned archaeologist with over 40 years of experience. A graduate of Muskingum University with an MBA from Point Park University and a Ph.D. in Anthropology from the University of Pittsburgh, she studied under Dr. James Adovasio, renowned for his work at Meadowcroft Rockshelter. Dr. Landers wrote her dissertation on Meadowcroft and later became an Associate Professor at Indiana University, where she developed the first archaeology program at the Fort Wayne campus.

Returning to Pittsburgh, she joined GAI Consultants, where she became the first female Vice President and Board Member. As a consulting archaeologist, she managed significant historic and prehistoric excavations, including projects in Pennsylvania, West Virginia, and at National Battlefields like Fort Necessity and Gettysburg.

Dr. Landers is also a native Pittsburgher with deep family ties to the city’s real estate development. She volunteers on the board of the Pittsburgh CLO and serves as Chair of the Meadowcroft Advisory Board, where she continues her work in archaeology.

event.description:
Image: Henry Koerner, American, 1915-1991; Oh Fearful Wonder of Man (detail), 1962, oil on canvas, 88 3/16 × 102 3/8 in. (224 × 260 cm); Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburgh, The Henry L. Hillman Fund, 81.68; © Henry Koerner. By permission

When Henry Koerner arrived in Pittsburgh from New York in 1952, the American art world was changing. Koerner, a Jewish refugee from Vienna, was known for his distinctive style of magical realism, which was quickly being overshadowed by the rise of abstract expressionism.

But in Pittsburgh, he found new inspiration. The city’s epic vistas, gritty characters, and unexpected encounters became rich subjects for his work, while Pittsburgh itself offered a place where his artistic practice could flourish.

To honor the 35th anniversary of Koerner’s death, the Rauh Jewish Archives will look back at his Pittsburgh career and look ahead to his enduring legacy through four unique perspectives:

  • A local art historian will explore Koerner’s career in Pittsburgh.
  • A member of Koerner’s family and fellow art historian will offer both a personal and professional perspective on his life and work.
  • A documentary filmmaker will examine Koerner’s story through the lens of film.
  • The preservationist who purchased Koerner’s iconic Squirrel Hill home will reflect on the importance of preserving his legacy for future generations.

Together, these perspectives will paint a fuller portrait of Koerner, his relationship with Pittsburgh, and the lasting impact of his work on the city.

This program is presented in partnership with Concept Art Gallery.

reserve tickets

Admission

This program is free with advance registration.

About the Speakers

Dr Alex Taylor is an historian of modern American art and visual culture at the University of Pittsburgh. His research strives to locate works of art within the histories of global capitalism, consumption, and mass media. His interests include transnational modernisms, studio practice, artistic self-fashioning, patrons and patronage, advertising, consumer cultures, and the intersections between artistic, political, and economic life.

Dr. Joseph Koerner is a son of Henry Koerner and chair of the Department of Art and Architecture at Harvard University, where he teaches the history of art and architecture from the late Middle Ages to the present, with a focus on Northern Renaissance art, Dutch seventeenth-century, European Romanticism, and German and Austrian Modernism.

William Murphy is the Director of Operations at the Postwar Gallery in Homewood and the editor of several documentary projects about Koerner and his work.

Caroline Boyce is a preservationist and curator. Since purchasing the Koerner House in Squirrel Hill in 2021, she has worked to preserve Koerner’s artistic legacy in Pittsburgh and abroad.

event.description:
This spooky season, join local historians Hollen Barmer and Miranda Crotsley to uncover the history hiding in your own house.

Learn how to follow the clues through historic maps, property records, newspapers, and more to reveal your home’s past – and the people who once called it home.

Whether you’ve heard a bump in the night, discovered a mysterious detail during renovations, or are just a little nebby about who lived there before you, Hollen and Miranda will show you how to conduct your own historical investigation.

Every house has a history. Are you brave enough to find out what happened in yours?

Admission

The program is $10 for non-members and $5 for History Center members with advance registration. The program will take place in the Detre Library & Archives on the museum’s sixth floor.

About the Speakers

Hollen Barmer and Miranda Crotsley are the co-founders of Land and Kin Collaborative, a business dedicated to history and genealogy for people and places. They have been working together on house histories and family tree mysteries since 2014, serving clients around Western Pennsylvania and the United States. Since 2022, they have presented public workshops and conducted consulting sessions on investigating house histories. In addition, they collaborate with partners to uncover, research, and present local history topics ranging from enslavement in 18th and 19th century Pittsburgh to mysterious explosions and sensational trials of the 1920s.

When they are not digging into the history of old houses or telling neighborhood stories, they work in fields that involve storytelling, investigation, and history. Miranda Crotsley is an educator and Program Coordinator in PA State Parks at Jennings Environmental Education Center where she researches and develops programming around park natural and cultural history including a reconstructed 1820s-era tavern inn, an original 19th century one-room schoolhouse, and a 20th century abandoned coal mine. Hollen Barmer is a strategic communications manager, working with technical researchers to tell the stories of their work.

event.description:
Join the Josh Gibson Foundation for its annual Negro League Baseball Symposium, “A Keystone Story: Pennsylvania’s Negro League Legacy,” hosted in partnership with the Franco Harris Sports Museum at the History Center.

The program will feature an all-star panel of baseball historians, including author Courtney Michelle Smith, Ph.D.; Rob Ruck, historian at the University of Pittsburgh; and Ted Knorr, founder of the Society for American Baseball Research’s Negro League Research Conference.

Ruck, a noted author who wrote “Sandlot Seasons: Sport in Black Pittsburgh,” will examine Pittsburgh’s outsized contributions to the Negro Leagues, including the legendary Homestead Grays and Pittsburgh Crawfords.

Knorr, a longtime Harrisburg-based baseball researcher who has spent more than 40 years studying and preserving the history of Negro League baseball in Central Pennsylvania, will explore the history of the Harrisburg Giants. The Giants’ star-studded roster included legends like Rap Dixon, Fats Jenkins, and Spottswood Poles, whose nicknames were only surpassed by their on-field play.

Dr. Smith, a Philadelphia-based historian, professor, and author of “Jackie Robinson: A Life in American History” will share the lively history of the Philadelphia area’s Negro League teams, including the compelling story of Ed Bolden, who ran the Hilldale Club and the Philadelphia Stars during the course of his 40-year career.

Admission

This program is free with advance registration. Tickets include access to the Franco Harris Sports Museum, which features a long-term exhibition on the history of Negro League baseball in Western Pa.

American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation will be available upon request. Please contact us at programs@heinzhistorycenter.org in advance to request accommodations.

This program is presented in partnership with America250PA, established by the Pennsylvania state legislature and Governor to plan, encourage, develop and coordinate the commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, Pennsylvania’s integral role in that event, and the impact of its people on the nation’s past, present, and future.

Josh Gibson Foundation
The Josh Gibson Foundation believes in the endless possibilities for potential in today’s youth. By providing academic and athletic programs that foster leadership and scholarship, the skills necessary for tomorrow’s successes are created today. Its goal is to carry on the legacy of greatness and accomplishment embodied by Josh Gibson, by developing programs that help children of every level of ability reach their potential, and to create opportunities that set The Josh Gibson Foundation apart from other organizations and provides value for our communities. Learn more at joshgibson.org.

About the Speakers

Courtney Michelle Smith, Ph.D., is a historian, published author, and an avid baseball fan. Her love of baseball began in her childhood when she watched Phillies games narrated by Harry Kalas. She has retained her love for the Phillies, through all the highs and lows, and learned that she could combine her love of baseball and local history while taking a college course on Baseball & the American Tradition. That course came around the time of the 50th anniversary of Jackie Robinson’s debut with the Brooklyn Dodgers and introduced her to the history of Negro League Baseball. Her research focus on Ed Bolden, the Philadelphia Stars, and Black baseball in the Philadelphia area began over twenty years ago and led to the publication of her first book. She earned her B.A. in History and Political Science at Cabrini College and her M.A. and Ph.D. in American History Lehigh University. She lives in Delaware County, PA with her family.

Ted Knorr is a longtime Harrisburg‑based baseball researcher who has spent more than forty years studying and preserving the history of Negro League baseball in Central Pennsylvania. A retired Pennsylvania state administrator, he has devoted his post‑career life to documenting overlooked players, recovering lost box scores, and helping families and communities reconnect with their baseball heritage. Knorr founded Negro League Nights in Harrisburg, Lancaster, and York, as well as the Society for American Baseball Research’s Negro League Research Conference, now known as the Jerry Malloy Negro League Conference. His writing has appeared in SABR publications, local game programs, and newspapers, and, currently, in the online Truth Seekers Journal. He is best known for his extensive scholarship on Rap Dixon, the Georgia‑born, Steelton‑raised outfielder he has championed as a deserving Hall of Fame candidate. For the Josh Gibson Foundation’s Pennsylvania Negro League seminar, Knorr represents Harrisburg with a perspective shaped by local memory, regional pride, and decades of hands‑on research.

Rob Ruck is an historian at the University of Pittsburgh, where he teaches and writes about sport. He focuses on how people use sport to tell a collective story about who they are—to themselves and to the world.

His books include “Sandlot Seasons: Sport in Black Pittsburgh” (1987), “The Tropic of Baseball: Baseball in the Dominican Republic” (1991), “Rooney: A Sporting Life” (2010) which he wrote with his late wife, Maggie Jones Patterson, “Raceball: How the Major Leagues Colonized the Black and Latin Game” (2011), and “Tropic of Football: The Long and Perilous Journey of Samoans to the NFL” (2018). His most recent, co-authored books are “Pittsburgh Rising: From Frontier Town to Steel City” with Ted Muller and “Mal Goode Reporting: The Life and Work of a Black Broadcast Trailblazer,” with Liann Tsoukas.

His documentaries, “Kings on the Hill: Baseball’s Forgotten Men” (NBC 1995) and “The Republic of Baseball: Dominican Giants of the American Game” (2006) appeared on PBS. A member of the 2006 Hall of Fame special election committee for black and Latin players, he collaborated with the Hall of Fame on a permanent exhibit about Latinos in baseball – Viva Beisbol! – as well as Souls of The Game: The Voices of Black Baseball, which opened in Cooperstown in 2024.

America250PA and Lecture250

This program is part of the History Center’s year-long commemoration of the U.S. Semiquincentennial, marking the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence, in partnership with America250PA.

The Lecture250 Series, hosted at partner locations across the Commonwealth in 2026, examines the forces that shaped Pennsylvania’s role in the American story—from the founding ideals of independence and equality to the development of industry, culture, community identity, and global connections. Each event will include a public discussion following the lecture to deepen civic engagement and invite community reflection.

Heinz History Center programs commemorating America’s 250th anniversary are supported by Nimick Forbesway Foundation, Richard King Mellon Foundation, Visit PA, and the Allegheny Regional Asset District (RAD).

Join us after hours on the third Thursday of every month for an evening at the History Center!

Grab a drink from the cash bar and explore six floors of award-winning exhibitions.

Whether you’re unwinding after work, planning a date night, or gathering with friends, Third Thursdays offer a fresh way to experience the #1 History Museum in America.

Admission

Third Thursdays are included with regular admission and offer access to the Heinz History Center for the entire day (10 a.m. to 8 p.m.). Kids aged 17 and under always receive free admission, supported by the Kamin “Free for Kids” Initiative.

Have an Allegheny County library card?

Register for a RAD Pass to enjoy Third Thursdays for FREE.

event.description:
Every First Friday the Lancaster Science Factory offers free admission from 5 – 7pm for the first 300 guests. Explore over 80 interactive exhibits for kids in grades K – 8 and their families! This program is possible through the generous support of PPL.

Manufacturing First Friday is sponsored by ManTec! There will be fun, hands-on, manufacturing themed activities all over the museum, including Make 717 and robotics team One Small Step for an Axolotl!

Lancaster Science Factory will be closing at 4:00pm on Friday, October 2 to allow for vendor set up. We will reopen at 5:00pm for the event!

All children must be accompanied by an adult. To make the most of your experience, we recommend 1 adult for every 5 kids during your First Friday visit.

event.title: Night Owls
event.description:
Night Owls 

Friday October 9th, 2026, 5:00 – 8:00 PM 

Experience an evening of science and discovery after dark at the Lancaster Science Factory. 

Explore the Science Factory, enjoy special owl-themed activities, and learn all about these fascinating nocturnal animals. 

Live Owl Presentations 

Presented by Raven Ridge Wildlife Center 

Join us for a special live owl presentation featuring Horus and Khonsu. 

Showtimes: 

  • 5:30 PM 
  • 6:15 PM 
  • 7:00 PM 

Owl presentation tickets are $3 per person in addition to general admission. Lancaster Science Factory members receive 10% off the owl presentation ticket. 

Space is limited, so advance tickets are recommended. 

More Owl Activities 

Throughout the evening, enjoy additional owl-themed activities included with your admission. 

Owl Pellet Investigation
Discover what an owl has been eating by examining real owl pellets and uncovering the clues inside. 

Science Café
Get hands-on with real owl specimens and discover how wings, feet, and skulls help owls survive and thrive. 

Plus, explore all of your favorite Lancaster Science Factory exhibits throughout the evening. 

General admission is required to attend Night Owls. Owl presentation tickets are sold separately.

Tickets on sale now!

11:00 Tickets

event.title: Science in ACTION! with Millersville University Chemistry Club
event.description:
Get ready for chemistry to come alive!

Join the Millersville University Chemistry Club for exciting live demonstrations that turn science into a show. Explore surprising reactions, cool chemistry, and plenty of WOW moments as you discover what happens when chemistry is put into action!

event.title: A Taste of Science
event.description:
A TASTE OF SCIENCE: It’s the Biggest Science Party of the Year!

Thursday, October 22th from 6:00pm- 9:00pm

Join us for A Taste of Science- an evening of entertainment, food, drinks, and science – all to benefit Lancaster Science Factory! This event helps us meet our mission to inspire curiosity, creativity, and confidence in young learners. Help us ensure our hands-on STEM experiences are accessible to all students across Lancaster County. This is a 21+ event.

Learn more about our nonprofit mission.

Tickets available now!! $70!

 

If your business is interested in supporting A Taste of Science, click here for more information about sponsorship. If you are interested in contributing a silent auction or raffle item, click here for our contribution form and contact rreed@tlsf.org to coordinate pick up or drop off.

 

YOUR TICKET INCLUDES:

  • Live Science Trivia hosted by Drew’s Clues – participate in a team of up to 8 people!
  • Dinner catered by Frisco’s Peruvian Chicken – vegetarian options available!
  • Dessert provided by Nothing Bundt Cakes.
  • Science-themed cocktails curated and served by Lancaster’s Thistle Finch Distillery.
  • Beer tasing with Lancaster Brewers Club.
  • Lots of prizes and surprises, plus time to explore our hands-on exhibits throughout the Science Factory!

Want to give additional support to hands-on STEM education in our community? This event will also feature a raffle and silent auction.

We would like to extend a heartfelt thank you to our sponsors:

 

Check out some highlights from previous A Taste of Science events!

event.title: Night Shift at Lancaster Science Factory
event.description:
Night Shift 2026-27 

Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. New to this year, educators will be leading hands-on STEM workshops in our Maker Space! Consider joining us for the Night Shift with your scout group, sports team or even for a special birthday! 

Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.

event.title: VCU Living Lab Research Demos – Downtown
event.description:
VCU psychology students, under the guidance of Dr. Marcia Winter, conduct research demonstrations on the museum floor, sharing insights from studies done through the National Living Lab network. Later in the semester, students will also conduct a live research study on children’s pre-writing skills with families who provide consent, coordinated by Dr. Virginia Chu from VCU’s Department of Occupational Therapy.

Visitors are welcome to stop by to observe the demonstrations and learn about the research process and, if interested, participate in a one-on-one live study.

Please note: This is not a general museum activity. Participation in the live study is one-on-one and limited to one family at a time. Visitors are welcome to stop by to observe the demonstrations and learn about the research process.

Immerse yourself in the vibrant traditions and experience a special performance through an engaging cultural presentation. It’s a fun and educational way to explore a different culture.
Who’s It For?
Ideal for families and children of all ages.
Cost
Free with Museum admission.

No pre-registration is required for this program. Please arrive early to ensure your spot! This event is held in partnership with Culture Encounters.

This class is designed to be unique to CMoR and was created with all kids in mind! We can’t wait to move with you!

event.description:
Jim Henson’s musical, fun-loving Fraggles are dancing their
cares away across North America and coming to Scranton in Jim Henson’s Fraggle
Rock: Back to the Rock LIVE, the first-ever live touring show based on The Jim Henson
Company’s beloved franchise.

Gobo, Red, Mokey, Wembley, and Boober Fraggle discover the legend of the Celebration
Stone – an ancient Fraggle treasure that has the power to bring everyone together for the
greatest party of all time, but was shattered and lost generations ago. As the Fraggles set
off on an exhilarating, adventurous journey exploring exciting new caves within Fraggle
Rock and even beyond, they discover magic that they never knew existed, and learn to
work together to unite the lost pieces of the magical artifact. Can the Fraggles succeed in
their quest to bring the Celebration Stone back to Fraggle Rock so everyone can enjoy the
most incredible party in Fraggle history? And along the way, will they find something even
more memorable and heartfelt than they could have ever imagined?

Based on the Emmy-winning Apple TV original series Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock, this
all-new, family friendly live stage adventure features colorful new walkaround versions of
the Fraggles, new puppet versions of their industrious friends the Doozers, and a visit from
a giant Gorg, as well as exciting original puppet creature friends – all built by the renowned
Jim Henson’s Creature Shop. Featuring fan-favorite songs and exciting visual effects, this
musical stage adventure welcomes audiences on a joyful, nostalgia-filled trip to Fraggle
Rock. With lots of music, laughter and imagination, it’s an unforgettable live experience
that will have Silly Creatures of all ages dancing in the aisles!

Written and directed by John Tartaglia (Avenue Q, Shrek the Musical, Stephen
Schwartz’s The Secret Silk), the interactive live musical features both new and classic
Fraggle songs, eye-popping immersive stage effects and all the hilarious, heartwarming
magic that has kept Fraggle Rock captivating generations of audiences for over 40 years.
Fraggle Rock: Back to the Rock LIVE is produced by The Jim Henson Company with
Catalyst Theatricals LLC acting as General Manager and Broadway & Beyond Theatricals as
the show’s exclusive booking agency. Visit www.fragglerocklive.com for more information.

The Band Perry

The Band Perry is a GRAMMY®, CMA, and ACM Award-winning band known for their genre-defying sound and bold artistic reinvention. Since bursting onto the scene with their 9x Platinum smash hit “If I Die Young,” the Band, led by the artistic eye and creative direction of lead singer / songwriter, Kimberly, have captivated audiences worldwide. The band’s 2025 return marks the end of hiatus and the start of the band’s next era.

Spanning a decade-plus of music and two albums, The Band Perry has sold two and a half million albums, 12 million singles, and racked up over 1 billion streams. Their success story continues to grow both domestically and globally, a talent powerhouse touting sold-out world tours, six #1 singles, multiple RIAA Platinum and Gold certifications, and pioneering chart success. Their Appalachian gothic sound is amplified by heartfelt, original storytelling, dynamic musicianship, and high-energy performance. Known for pushing creative boundaries while staying rooted in Southern tradition, the band continues to evolve, both artistically and as individuals.

 

Kameron Marlowe

While working as a car parts salesman in Kannapolis, Marlowe received a call from a talent recruiter from The Voice who had seen his live performance videos on YouTube. They offered Marlowe a fast track to the series’ live auditions. He debuted on the show’s Blind Auditions premiere on September 24, 2018. Subsequently, he joined Blake Shelton‘s Team Blake before being “stolen” by coach Adam Levine later in the season. He was eliminated in the Live Playoffs Top 24 episode on November 13, 2018. Subsequently, Marlowe moved to Nashville, Tennessee to pursue a career as a songwriter.

 

Charles Wesly Godwin

When you release a project like Charles Wesley Godwin’s 2023 critically acclaimed Family Ties — a highly personal, 17-song diary-like LP that was both universally praised and also catapulted the West Virginian singer-songwriter to new heights in his career — the outside perception is that there are greater expectations on whatever music comes next. Ask Godwin, however, and he’ll tell you that instead of dwelling on any chatter that accompanied such a revered release, he did what he always has done: Godwin simply kept on writing. “I’ve learned from the past that it’s not good to stop,” says the singer-songwriter — a humble songsmith whose music is deeply felt, undeniably intimate, and, over the past few years, has been connecting with audiences in ways he could have never imagined when he began his career just over a decade ago. “The more consistent I am and the more I’m putting in the time and effort into my songwriting, the more the songs come and the more I’m able to be productive.”

For Charles Wesley Godwin, music — and more specifically, songwriting — has forever been a direct reflection of what lies on his heart. 2019’s Seneca is a young man’s reflection on place, on upbringing, on a way of life that is and always will be his native West Virginia. 2021’s How the Mighty Fall is a treatise on mortality and the contemporary, commonplace entanglements that threaten to derail us. 2023’s fan-favorite Family Ties is an equal-parts tribute to and dissection of complex, albeit achingly beautiful, familial dynamics. And now, with Christian Name, Godwin’s much-anticipated fourth full-length studio LP, the musician returns with his most vividly compelling, stunningly sincere, and spiritually profound collection of songs yet.

As Godwin now prepares to unveil this highly intimate and personal Christian Name, the singer-songwriter says he’s never been more content with where things stand.

“This album, more than any other, I’m at peace with whatever happens going forward,” Godwin says. “I prayed on this album a lot. And I truly believe there’s a purpose to all this.”

 

McCoy Moore

With a style rooted in the charm of his Central-Florida home, Sony Music Entertainment’s McCoy Moore makes country music so radiant and relaxed it should come with SPF 50. Through beaming baritone vocals and a warm sonic glow, the singer-songwriter embodies the land of perpetual summer, complete with its easy-does-it code of humble sincerity. On his debut album, Sunshine State, the Lakeland native shows Florida is much more than a vacation destination – it’s the place that made him the artist he is.

A lifelong country fan schooled on late ‘90s and early 2000s radio, Kenny Chesney (his first concert), Tim McGraw, and Keith Whitley were the soundtrack to travel baseball and day trips to the beach, before a chance encounter with Luke Combs in 2017 helped propel Moore to Nashville at 19 years old. Wrapping nostalgic real-life stories in a rich, resonate country baritone, he began releasing music in 2025 with tracks like “Something to You,” and has now accumulated more than 17 million global streams while touring with HARDY, Kip Moore, and Chase Rice.

But his heart remains in the Sunshine State. Co-writing all but one of 14 songs produced by hit maker Will Bundy (Riley Green, Ella Langley, Thomas Rhett), modern muscle and a throwback country spirit tap the nostalgic heat of long gone summers, while Moore’s vocal carries the buzz of an incoming thunderhead. Heavy bass lines and steel guitars hang thick like Spanish Moss off an old Live Oak (much like the one on the album’s cover, which was shot in his grandparents’ garage), with soaring emotions and bright melodies begging to be cranked up loud. Over and over, vivid memories transform into singalong revelations of Moore’s Sunshine State.

It’s just where he comes from.

 

Atlus

Raised in a single-parent home marked by poverty and addiction, Atlus had to grow up fast, building incredible resilience and laying the foundation for a life rooted in the search for authentic relationships and honest storytelling. Phonetically named after the mythological Titan who held up the heavens, Atlus wrote his first two (of four) albums while working as a commercial driver behind the wheel of semi-trucks, using the long, lonesome miles of highway to craft lyrics and workshop melodies as he drove countless hours to help support his family and fund studio time.

That pavement-pounding lifestyle became both his education and his engine. Over time, it helped grow his underground following and ultimately led to breakout moments like performing alongside Jelly Roll at a packed Red Rocks Amphitheatre in his home state, and landing a Top 5 album on Spotify’s Global Album Chart, along with a Platinum single. The magic of Atlus lies in how he marries candid, arresting, and often dark subjects with a kaleidoscope of sound. His music blends multiple styles into something fresh and immersive, anchored by storytelling that creates a deep connection with fans. Now with over a billion on-demand streams and two million followers across socials, Atlus continues to build his career on real connection and resilience. He’s holding up his musical dreams in support of his family and anyone who turns to music as an outlet for their own struggles. Signed to BBR Music group/BMG Nashville, his debut release on the label, “Devil Ain’t Done” is available now.

event.description: SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. event.description:
ONE NIGHT ONLY — A must-see theatrical event.

Experience the world’s most beloved ballet like never before. International Ballet Stars returns with a breathtaking production set to Tchaikovsky’s iconic score and performed by a world-class international cast representing four continents. From the moonlit lakeside where Princess Odette is held under a powerful spell, to the dazzling royal ballroom where the seductive Odile delivers the legendary 32 fouettés – every scene is filled with drama, precision, and unforgettable beauty.

This large-scale, immersive, Broadway-caliber production brings together over 150 handcrafted costumes, richly detailed sets, and an exceptional company of dancers to create a spectacular live experience. Elegant, emotional, and visually stunning, Swan Lake is more than a ballet – it is a night at the theater you will remember long after the final curtain. A timeless story of love, betrayal, and redemption, captivating audiences of all generations.

The dazzling cast of IBS representing 16 countries, including Spain, Brazil, Poland, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, Italy, Austria, Georgia, Iceland, Japan, Moldova, Romania, Belarus, Armenia, Mongolia, and Albania – make this a truly global celebration of dance.

Artistic Direction: Artem Yachmennikov – Former Principal Dancer, San Francisco Ballet & Dutch National Ballet.

For more info on the cast, synopsis and FAQ, visit: internationalballetstars.com

event.description: The original Broadway sensation returns to the road! Celebrating 20 years – Jersey style! They were just four guys from Jersey, until they sang their very first note. They had a sound nobody had ever heard… and the radio just couldn’t get enough of. But while their harmonies were perfect on stage, off stage it was a very different story — a story that has made them a international sensation all over again. The show features all their hits including “Sherry,” “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” “Oh What a Night,” “Walk Like a Man,” “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” “Beggin’” and “Working My Way Back to You.” Go behind the music and inside the story of Frankie Valli and The Four Seasons in the Tony Award®-winning, original Broadway sensation, JERSEY BOYS.
